description:
✈️ Babylon Flight 737
A fully-featured, browser-based 3D flight simulator built entirely with HTML, CSS, and vanilla JavaScript using the Babylon.js engine.

Originally a 9,000-line monolith, this project has been heavily optimized for performance, featuring lazy-loading for aircraft models, progressive satellite terrain streaming, and a custom resolution manager.

🌟 Features
50+ Aircraft: Fly everything from the Cessna 172 to the Airbus A380 and Concorde.

Career Mode: Earn money and XP, unlock new planes in the Hangar, and complete generated missions and flight lessons.

Dynamic Imagery: Streams real-world satellite imagery (ESRI/Google) and 3D elevation data.

Advanced Systems: Fully functional Autopilot, FMS map with waypoints, and ATC voice clearances.

Failure Simulation: Inject 40+ faults (engine fires, sensor failures, rapid decompression) via the UI or keyboard.

Flight Physics: Custom aerodynamic physics engine, including ground effect, stall buffeting, bounce physics, and crash debris/replay.

🚀 How to Play
GitHub Pages: You can play the live version hosted on this repository's GitHub Pages.

Locally: Because the game fetches external satellite data, you cannot just double-click index.html (browsers block local CORS requests). You must run a local web server.

VS Code: Install the Live Server extension and click "Go Live".

Python: Run python -m http.server in the folder, then open http://localhost:8000.

🎮 Basic Controls
Key	Action
W / S	Pitch (Nose down / up)
A / D	Roll (Left / right)
Q / E	Rudder (Yaw)
Shift / Ctrl	Throttle up / down
G	Landing Gear up / down
F	Flaps
C or V	Cycle Camera (Chase, Cockpit, Flyby)
P	Autopilot (Hold HDG & ALT)
J	Open FMS / Map
K	Open ATC Radio
(For a full list of controls, including trim and liveries, open the "Controls & Key Bindings" dropdown on the main menu).

⚡ Performance Note
The game includes a Resolution Dropdown on the main menu. If the game is loading too slowly on a school or public network, change the imagery setting to "Low" or "Medium". The game will start flying immediately while the satellite map streams in the background.
